subject.title: [Feature]: Intelligent Model Fallback with Wildcard/Auto Selection

question: Should OpenClaw add a provider-family fallback contract here, and if so should it be wildcard/auto refs, explicit grouped fallback families, catalog-derived fallback derivation, or a narrower combination?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the remaining choice defines public config semantics for provider/model routing, cost, auth behavior, and upgrade expectations.

options.title: Design one fallback-family contract
options.body: Pick one canonical config shape and require schema, runtime, docs, and migration/doctor alignment before implementation.

options.title: Narrow to catalog-derived fallback
options.body: Treat the open catalog-derived fallback PR as the only supported direction and leave wildcard/auto and grouped families out of scope.

options.title: Keep explicit fallbacks only
options.body: Decline new fallback config surface and direct users to maintain ordered fallback lists manually.

recommendation.title: Design one fallback-family contract
recommendation.body: Pick one canonical config shape and require schema, runtime, docs, and migration/doctor alignment before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter has the strongest recent history across model fallback behavior, schema/config surfaces, and product-scope fallback decisions.
